title: A short history of the bicycle
paragraphs: The first widely used two-wheeled vehicle, the draisine, appeared in 1817. It had no pedals; the rider pushed along the ground with their feet. Pedals attached to the front wheel came in the 1860s, producing the heavy machine nicknamed the boneshaker.

The high-wheeled penny-farthing followed in the 1870s, fast but dangerous. The safety bicycle of the 1880s, with two wheels of equal size and a chain drive to the rear wheel, set the pattern that bicycles still follow today.
Pneumatic tires, introduced by John Dunlop in 1888, made riding far more comfortable, and by the 1890s a cycling craze had swept Europe and North America.
